chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), when it was morning, would go out early in search of livelihood. So it was said to him, 'O son of the Messenger of Allah, where are you going?' He said, 'To give charity to my dependents.' It was said to him, 'Do you give charity?' He said, 'The one who seeks the permissible (halal), it is a charity from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, upon him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for working to provide for one's family in Islam?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) illustrates the Shia scholarly view that seeking halal sustenance is an act of worship, transforming the mundane effort of provision into a spiritual charity. It underscores the dignity of labor, suggesting that the divine reward for providing for one's family is so significant that the effort itself is considered a gift from God, thereby elevating daily economic activity to the realm of ibadah.
